questions.q: What problem do WSUS and Windows Update for Business both solve, compared to every machine checking in with Microsoft on its own?
options: Wasted bandwidth and no central control over which updates go out and when
A requirement that every machine run Linux instead of Windows
Windows machines being unable to receive any updates at all without one of these tools
The complete removal of Patch Tuesday as a release schedule
questions.explain: Left unmanaged, every machine separately re-downloads the same updates and IT has no way to hold back or stagger specific updates.

questions.q: What is WSUS (Windows Server Update Services)?
options: A cloud-only service with no on-premises server component
A Windows Server role that downloads updates once and lets an admin approve/decline and target them to computer groups
A third-party antivirus product unrelated to Windows Update
A feature that only works on Linux servers
questions.explain: WSUS centralizes update distribution on a server administrators control, with explicit approval and group targeting.

questions.q: How does Windows Update for Business (WUfB) manage updates, as described in this lesson?
options: By completely disabling Patch Tuesday for enrolled devices
By requiring every machine to install a local WSUS server
Through cloud policy using deployment rings and deferral periods, with no on-premises server required
Only through manual approval of each individual update, identical to WSUS
questions.explain: WUfB is configured via Group Policy or an MDM platform like Intune, assigning devices to rings with different deferral periods instead of approving updates one at a time.

questions.q: In WUfB, what does a 14-day deferral period on the "Broad" ring actually do?
options: Permanently blocks that ring from ever receiving the update
Forces the update to install within 14 minutes of release
Delays installation of a released update on that ring by 14 days, giving the pilot ring time to surface problems first
Has no effect on install timing, only on notifications
questions.explain: Deferral periods delay installation by a set number of days after release, implementing a staged rollout without per-update approval.

questions.q: Based on this lesson, which environment is WSUS best suited for?
options: A traditional on-premises Active Directory environment where IT wants fine-grained, update-by-update control
Any environment with fewer than ten machines
A fully remote, cloud-managed fleet that rarely connects to the corporate network
Environments that have no Windows Server infrastructure at all
questions.explain: WSUS requires on-premises server infrastructure and machines that can reach it, which fits a traditional AD-joined network better than a remote, cloud-managed fleet.
